newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX backs away from 3,200 pts before Lent.
newsitem.headline: German DAX backs away from 3,200 pts before Lent.

text.p: German shares surrendered most of their earlier gains at the close of bourse trading on Tuesday as dealers said trading volumes were hit by the half-day pre-Lent holiday in Frankfurt.

The DAX-30 index of leading shares closed 3.22 points or 0.1 percent up at 3,187.58 after earlier reaching an all-time high of 3,196.41. March DAX futures were also off earlier highs, four points up at 3,197.0.
"We went up just a little too fast," said one Frankfurt dealer, noting that it had looked earlier in the day that the DAX was go through the psychologically-key 3,200-point level.
The retreat came despite a strong dollar, which moved past 1.67 marks, and with German debt futures pushing close to record levels.
Earlier, shares had shrugged off the negative impact of Wall Street's overnight losses, which were seen as largely to do with a sell-off in technology stocks .
German software group SAP, down 2.80 marks at 253.20, was thus the only real victim of the weaker Dow.

Drugs group Schering touched a new year-high of 146.20 in bourse trade after reporting better-than-expected net profit for 1996. It later dropped back to close at 145.40 marks, 2.20 marks up on the day.
Shares in machine tool-maker Traub were suspended in advance of a statement from the group saying that bankruptcy proceedings had, as expected, now started.
